judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'changes from the schedule now in use' measures the new schedule against an unidentified existing document, and the paragraph is tied to a 1970 agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-A.1 requires each Publisher to 'continue in effect the schedules shown in the last notice of such schedules to the Union for the duration of this contract,' which is in tension with issuing a new schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise page-size and bundle-count rule with no open terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must sit within 3-A.1's frozen schedules and 46-pound bundle ceiling, and 3-A.2's separate loads-per-truck schedules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'weighing 42 pounds or more' and '272 bundles per truck' are both exact.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-A.1 caps bundles at forty-six pounds, so this rule operates only in the 42-46 pound band — a narrow but real interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'bundle weight of 87 to 46 pounds' is impossible as written (evidently 37), and 'a reasonable number of bundles to facilitate efficient loading' is an open exception to a fixed maximum.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 46-pound upper figure matches 3-A.1's ceiling, so the misprint is internal to this paragraph rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, fully specified forbearance identifying the judgment by amount, action number and date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is qualified by paragraph 3's reservation of rights as to future incidents; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'will develop a stipulation providing for the withdrawal and vacation of the judgment' promises a document without specifying its terms or a deadline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with paragraph 1's forbearance; no contrary provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'because of the relationship which has developed' is a stated motive, and the reservation as to 'any future incident' is broad but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This recital of motive sits beside operative forbearance in paragraph 1, a mild recital-versus-operative pairing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An exact principal sum tied to a named arbitrator, award and work stoppage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the premise for the payment schedule in A and the acceleration clause in 3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'monthly installments of $1,250' against a principal of $177,844 implies roughly 142 months of payments, far beyond any stated end point, and no final date is given.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The October 26, 1981 letter says that 'when the six payments referred to in the Memorandum have been made ... The News will not, under any circumstances, require additional payments,' but this Memorandum provides for indefinite monthly installments, not six payments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line waiver of interest with nothing open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the installment schedule in A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'meet to review the payment schedule, the Union's ability to pay and other relevant factors' promises a meeting with no stated consequence, and 'other relevant factors' is a catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The companion letter's 'six payments' language would end the obligation around the same time this review falls due, which is hard to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'more favorable terms or treatment with respect to the payment or disposition called for by an arbitration award or judicial decree' is a broad comparison with no measuring rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The October 7, 1981 letter contains a differently drafted most-favoured-nation promise on benefits with express carve-outs, showing the parties used varying formulas.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific withdrawal of a named action on a defined trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with paragraph 1's payment arrangement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the provisions against strikes and disruptions of orderly relationships' is plural and the second phrase has no counterpart anywhere in the Agreement, so the acceleration trigger is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-N is the only no-strike clause and it contains an express exception permitting action against a party that fails to comply with a Board decision, which this acceleration clause does not acknowledge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any major change in its operations which has an impact on a significant number of its NMDU employees' contains two undefined thresholds, softened only by a single example.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.3 requires the other party's prior consent for any 'change in condition,' 5-J requires four days' notice of starting-time changes, and 20-E.2 requires notice of a Bulldog phase-out — four different notice/consent regimes for overlapping events.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The memorandum's content is a direction that an arbitrator 'render a written decision interpreting the language of Section 16-M' by reference to an unrecorded oral opinion and a 1971 award in a different union's arbitration — the meaning is deferred rather than stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is an express admission that Section 16-M's 'change in condition' language is unresolved, and it imports an outside decision as the governing gloss.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence — 'Every memorandum, letter agreement or side agreement shall be continued through the term of this agreement and deemed updated' — with 'deemed updated' wholly undefined and no list of what is continued.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be reconciled with 21-B.4's declared expiry in 1975, 21-D VIII's supersession of all Newspoint memoranda, or 17-D's statement that bargaining is settled for the term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This Supplementary Agreement is within the terms of the current collective bargaining agreement' asserts consistency without saying which terms govern in a clash.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its items 1, 3 and 4 alter Carlstadt manning and starting-time rights that 22-A and 5-J already address, so the asserted consistency is exactly what would be tested.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'one of 5 nights, and one of 4 days and one night, and one additional shift (a total of 11 shifts)' does not add up cleanly and leaves the eleventh shift's owner unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-A's Carlstadt Floor Operations paragraph sets only a minimum of one floor employee, and 21-D III fixes Newspoint manning differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'including but not limited to, relieving the console for breaks; clearing jams ...; handling wire machine breaks, etc.' is an open catch-all sitting in the same paragraph as an exclusive assignment ('may only be performed by the utility man').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-A's control-room paragraph gives the delivery department jurisdiction of console work and 2-I lets employers require any covered operation, both of which bear on this exclusivity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Should the number of men hired be reduced as herein set forth' refers back to a reduction the paragraph never sets forth, and 'people performing functions other than regular floor work' and 'provided all areas are properly manned' are undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves 'the obligation of The Times to hire from the shape in priority order in accordance with the Agreement,' so it must be squared with 4-A.2's hiring order and 22-A's floor minimum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The guarantee runs to 'all regular situation holders as of the date of this agreement' but is then limited to 'the named individuals' — and no individuals are named anywhere in the document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-J expressly contemplates changes in starting times on four days' notice and 20-E.7 puts starting times of excess situation holders 'at the discretion of the Publishers,' both of which this guarantee overrides for an uncertain class.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'an extra half hour at the required rate' does not say which rate is required, and 'if the starting point and finishing point are the same' is an unexplained carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-L addresses travel time generally and directs the parties to negotiate an arrangement, which this paragraph partly supplies for one situation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple document-delivery obligation fixed to the signing date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The October 26, 1981 posting letter separately commits both papers to posting job descriptions, overlapping this duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a "Blue Goose" (passenger vehicle) for use on [two named employees'] job' is terse and personal but the parenthetical defines the term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-K requires the Publisher to furnish all delivery equipment, which is consistent with this commitment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as it does during the week' incorporates existing weekday practice as the standard, which is not written down.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-E.2(e)(1) already requires Albany runs to be driven by covered employees through to the city, so the two provisions overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, dated commitment with a clear frequency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relates to 14-C's bad-driving-record discharges but does not conflict with anything.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such route shall be filed by in-shop bidding' says 'filed' where 'filled' is plainly meant, an error that changes the sentence's operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B prescribes a four-week posting and seniority-based filling procedure, which 'in-shop bidding' here abbreviates without explanation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'including, but not limited to' opens the list, and the closing sentence ('these practices do not limit either party's rights') largely cancels the commitment just made.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-J already requires the Publisher to furnish the chapel chairman a list of starting times and days off, and the Times Supplementary Agreement ¶6 requires job descriptions be given to the Chairman.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'whatever increase, however formulated' is unbounded, while the two carve-outs — 'in exchange for productivity improvements (as determined to the Union's reasonable satisfaction)' and 'diverted from the negotiated pattern package' — are opaque and undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-F.3 contains a different News-only most-favoured-nation pension clause ('taken in their entirety, are more favorable') and the News damage memorandum ¶1.D a third, so three inconsistent parity formulas coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'shall continue to serve in their present respective capacities, until the parties select a replacement' is clear as a holdover rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-G provides that 'the term of the permanent impartial chairmen designated under Section 16-M. shall terminate upon the expiration of this Agreement,' and 16-M.1 requires annual reselection — both cut against an open-ended holdover.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the list of arbitrators provided by Section 16-E.1' misidentifies the provision that creates the list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-E.2 is the list-creating provision and 16-E.3 sets fixed June 1 dates for striking names, which an open-ended holdover of the old list would displace.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise notice-triggered amendment right with the Union choosing between two stated frequencies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly amends 2-N.1, which as printed requires deduction 'from the second pay check of the employee in each month' — the operative text and this letter cannot both stand unaltered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Times is happy to continue our discussions and review of this subject' commits to nothing that could be enforced.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 17-D says the parties 'have settled the same for the term of this Agreement,' which sits oddly with a live commitment to keep discussing pension changes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'providing such transport did not involve the Times in increased costs' is an escape with no benchmark, and the letter only records that discussion was agreed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9-B uses the identical 'increased cost' escape for outside-printed sections, and 3-E freezes methods and extent of delivery — the Lancaster question falls between them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If a sufficient number of employees are interested' makes the whole programme conditional on an unquantified threshold, and the bank is 'Citibank (or another acceptable bank)' without saying acceptable to whom.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-N.2 subjects deductions to Section 302 of the LMRA, and the credit-union letter uses a written-assignment mechanism this letter omits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All trucks used for over-the-road runs (Long Island routes, news company runs, all other long runs)' closes an enumerated list with the undefined 'all other long runs.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-H.1 requires that within thirty days 'all motor vehicles shall be equipped with heaters and defrosters,' a broader duty than this letter's under-the-seat heater commitments for new and remaining News trucks.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'When the six payments referred to in the Memorandum have been made' identifies a set of six payments, and 'will not, under any circumstances, require additional payments' is absolute yet immediately qualified by the reservation that follows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Memorandum of Understanding it refers to provides for open-ended '$1,250' monthly installments against $177,844, never six payments, so the two documents describe different bargains.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The letter is printed out of order and its last words trail off ('The News will abide by all Newspoint written agreements' appears above the sentence it follows), and '48 inch height from the top of the skid' incorporates an unquoted award.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D VIII says the Newspoint agreement 'supersedes and replaces all other agreements, memoranda or practices ... applicable to the Newspoint operation,' which is difficult to reconcile with a promise to abide by all Newspoint written agreements and awards.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'should there be a problem in the future arising thereunder, such Memorandum shall be applicable' revives a deleted document on an undefined trigger ('a problem') and never states its content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinstates a memorandum from the 1978-81 agreement that the parties deliberately deleted, which cuts against 17-D's settled-bargaining clause and complicates the blanket continuation memorandum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the Medill Plan' is almost certainly a misprint for the Medical Plan, and no rules of eligibility are stated — only a promise to post them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-H governs the Welfare Fund and 22-G The Times' insurance, so which plan's eligibility is meant is not resolvable from the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'for a reasonable period of time designated by the employee' and 'a written assignment satisfactory to the Publisher' are two open standards in one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-N.1 and 2-N.2 govern payroll deductions and subject them to Section 302 of the LMRA, which this deduction must also satisfy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'prohibits the subcontracting of bargaining unit deliveries except as it may exist pursuant to the contract' is circular — the exception is defined by the contract the letter purports to clarify — and 'subcontracting' appears nowhere in the Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-E freezes methods and extent, 3-F gives free choice on new routes, 2-E.2(h) permits discontinuing over-the-road trucking, and 12-A conditions distribution through wholesalers — the letter asserts a prohibition none of them states in terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'continue its present practice' incorporates an unstated practice, though the annual statement duty is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-B already governs Times vacation checks and deductions, and the News DEC letter states a different, condition-based version of the same commitments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three of the four commitments are conditioned on 'when the planned DEC System is installed and operational' with no deadline, and 'credited shifts for which contributions were not made' is a puzzling category.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-I.1 fixes contributions on 'each shift worked' with a five-shift cap, so a statement of credited shifts for which no contribution was made presupposes a gap the operative text does not describe.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'except if delayed because of an emergency or Act of God' pairs a broad general term with a specific one, leaving the excuse's reach open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It implements the 13-A.1 first-year increase effective March 31, 1981; no conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Incident to the negotiation of the present Collective Bargaining Committee' is garbled, and 'discussed and agreed upon the following' introduces items that are largely reports of discussion rather than agreements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The letter is dated November 3, 1978 yet printed in the 1981-84 agreement, and the blanket continuation memorandum deems side agreements 'updated' without saying how.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Union requested that the Company order vans with side doors and was advised that such vans would be ordered' records a statement rather than making a promise — whether it binds anyone is genuinely arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its preamble says the parties 'agreed upon the following,' which sits against the purely narrative form of this item.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'would explore the purchase and use of dehumidifiers' is an obligation to consider, not to act, and 'concern regarding conditions' is unspecified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-H.1's undue-hardship duty covers plant conditions generally, so this item adds little but is not contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'three-part inserts (500 or more)' does not say 500 or more of what, and 'paid the same as the men in the New York plant' incorporates an unstated rate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-A sets uniform scales for all covered employees, which makes a plant-to-plant parity commitment somewhat redundant or in tension with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Company indicated that new trucks had been ordered' is a pure statement of fact with no promissory language at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The introductory line says the parties 'agreed upon the following,' so a purely factual recitation is difficult to characterise as an operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '"sixers"' is undefined trade shorthand and 'in the same percentage as they are currently available' pegs the entitlement to an unrecorded baseline.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D governs Newspoint conditions comprehensively and VIII purports to supersede other Newspoint memoranda, which raises a question about this item's status.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of five named jobs to be 'defined when posted (Job Clarification)' — clear as to which jobs, silent as to what the definitions must contain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B and 21-D VII require posting of situations, and the job-description letter covers posting content, so three provisions bear on the same act.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'agreed to meet and discuss the printing of commercial sheets' creates no substantive obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D V already allocates commercial work at Newspoint, so what remains to be discussed is unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'meet within thirty (30) days to discuss shop level problems' is time-specific but substantively empty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-A already requires plant-level settlement attempts before referral, so this duplicates existing machinery.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble is garbled with stray characters and misdescribes the body as 'the present Collective Bargaining Committee' rather than agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Dated November 3, 1978 but printed in the 1981-84 contract and swept up by the blanket continuation memorandum, its currency is uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Two new console jobs will be created at the Carlstadt facility (one day job; one night job)' is fully specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-A's control-room paragraph and the Times Supplementary Agreement's utility-man provision both address Carlstadt console manning, so three provisions govern the same positions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The run's days, start time and bidding method are all stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Inter-shop bidding sits alongside 4-B's posting procedure and 22-A III's Philadelphia inter-shop bidding provision, consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'within a reasonable time after ratification of the contract, but in no event later than sixty (60) days' promises a review with no standard for its outcome.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'ratification of the contract' in a November 1978 letter reprinted in the 1981-84 agreement is ambiguous as to which ratification starts the clock.
